title: Short Words Preface Author Invocation Praise Blessings And The Eight Words

questions.question: What is the first thing said in the passage?
questions.answer: It begins by mentioning Allah’s name.

questions.question: Which two qualities of Allah are named in the English part?
questions.answer: Mercy and compassion.

questions.question: What does the passage say people ask Allah for?
questions.answer: Help.

questions.question: Who is called the Lord and Sustainer of all the worlds?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: Upon whom are blessings and peace sent?
questions.answer: Upon Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his companions.

questions.question: Why does the speaker say he will share a few truths?
questions.answer: Because someone asked him for some advice.

questions.question: How many short stories are mentioned?
questions.answer: Eight.

questions.question: What kind of examples are these stories said to be?
questions.answer: They are comparisons related to military life.

questions.question: Who does the speaker say needs the advice most?
questions.answer: His own nafs, meaning his own self.

questions.question: In what style will the speaker now address his nafs?
questions.answer: Briefly and in simple language ordinary people can understand.

questions.question: What important phrase opens the passage in Arabic and English?
questions.answer: A statement beginning in Allah’s name.

questions.question: Besides Allah’s name, what else is included near the beginning?
questions.answer: Praise to Allah and prayers for peace and blessings on Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his companions.

questions.question: What did the other person want from the speaker?
questions.answer: A small amount of advice.

questions.question: What form will the advice take?
questions.answer: It will come through eight short stories that compare things.

questions.question: Why are the comparisons connected to soldiers?
questions.answer: Because the person being spoken to is a soldier.

questions.question: What does the speaker admit about himself?
questions.answer: He says he himself needs advice more than anyone else.

questions.question: What inspired the longer advice he gave before?
questions.answer: Eight verses from the Qur’an.

questions.question: How is the new advice different from the earlier one?
questions.answer: This time it will be shorter and easier to understand.

questions.question: Who is invited to listen along with the speaker?
questions.answer: Anyone who wishes to listen.

questions.question: What does the passage teach us to do before giving advice or speaking?
questions.answer: Begin by remembering Allah and asking Him for help.

questions.question: What is Allah praised as being for all creation?
questions.answer: The Lord and caretaker of all worlds.

questions.question: What special respect is shown to Prophet Muhammad in the passage?
questions.answer: Prayers for blessings and peace are sent upon him.

questions.question: Which other people are included with Prophet Muhammad in that prayer?
questions.answer: His family and companions.

questions.question: What was the speaker asked to give?
questions.answer: Some words of advice.

questions.question: What number helps organize the advice in the passage?
questions.answer: The number eight.

questions.question: What does the speaker call the lessons inside those stories?
questions.answer: Truths.

questions.question: Why might military comparisons fit the listener well?
questions.answer: Because the listener is a soldier.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about advising others and advising yourself?
questions.answer: A person should also apply the advice to his own self.

questions.question: What does the opening teach about how a Muslim should begin something good?
questions.answer: By starting with Allah’s name.

questions.question: What three actions come near the start of the passage toward Allah and His Messenger?
questions.answer: Asking Allah for help, praising Allah, and sending blessings and peace on the Prophet.

questions.question: What does the speaker call his own inner self?
questions.answer: His nafs.

questions.question: According to the passage, how strongly does the speaker feel his need for guidance?
questions.answer: He feels he needs it more than anyone else.

questions.question: What source benefited the speaker before and led to a longer set of words?
questions.answer: Verses from the Qur’an.

questions.question: How many earlier “Words” had he addressed to himself?
questions.answer: Eight.

questions.question: Why does the speaker now choose simpler language?
questions.answer: So ordinary people can understand it more easily.

questions.question: Is the advice only for one person? Explain.
questions.answer: No. Although one person asked, anyone may listen and benefit.

questions.question: Who is the passage mainly praising at the beginning?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say Allah provides for all creation?
questions.answer: Care and sustaining for all the worlds.

questions.question: What is requested from Allah right away?
questions.answer: Help.

questions.question: What honor is given to Prophet Muhammad?
questions.answer: A prayer for blessings and peace.

questions.question: What kind of request started this whole talk?
questions.answer: A request for advice.

questions.question: How are the truths arranged so they can be taught clearly?
questions.answer: They are placed into eight short stories.

questions.question: What makes these stories especially suitable for the listener?
questions.answer: They use soldier-like examples that match his life.

questions.question: How were the earlier lessons and the new lessons connected?
questions.answer: Both deal with the same eight teachings.

questions.question: What does the final invitation to listen show about the audience?
questions.answer: The message is open to everyone who wants to benefit.

questions.question: What sacred habit appears at the very start of the passage?
questions.answer: Beginning in the name of Allah.

questions.question: Which qualities of Allah in the English line help us understand His care?
questions.answer: He is described as merciful and compassionate.

questions.question: What does the phrase about seeking help teach us about people?
questions.answer: It teaches that people need Allah’s help.

questions.question: How is Allah described in relation to every world and every creature?
questions.answer: He is their Lord and Sustainer.

questions.question: Name the three groups connected with the prayer for blessings and peace.
questions.answer: Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his companions.

questions.question: What was the speaker planning to give after the opening praises and prayers?
questions.answer: A few pieces of advice.

questions.question: What teaching method does the speaker choose for those lessons?
questions.answer: Short stories with comparisons.

questions.question: Why does the speaker mention being inspired by Qur’anic verses?
questions.answer: To show that the advice is connected to guidance from the Qur’an.

questions.question: What change does the speaker make in the way he will present the advice now?
questions.answer: He will make it shorter and use everyday language.
